source.title: CNN-Based Retinal OCT Classification: Research Gap Analysis and a From-Scratch Baseline, ED126-A

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for a from-scratch CNN on retinal OCT, extending the training-error finding to a different dataset and task.
record.gate_note: The study reports ED126-A training accuracy at selected epochs. Results cited from other OCT studies are not rows. It does not test CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted or random labels, or the effects of model size, depth, shortcuts, or initialization choices.
record.test_reason: The study reports training classification accuracy for a randomly initialized CNN on retinal OCT, providing a new-setting test of V1. It does not compare optimization methods or isolate architecture, initialization, or normalization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present ED126-A as a documented from-scratch OCT reference baseline, report 95.03% image-level held-out test accuracy, and identify Drusen false-positive assignments as the principal residual error pattern. They do not conclude that training reaches zero error or isolate causal optimization effects.
record.recipe_differences: Trains one compact CNN from scratch on four-class retinal OCT with AdamW, balanced class weights, augmentation, and early stopping; the claim versions concern CIFAR classification and other specified methods and conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy increased across the reported epochs; the best-validation-loss checkpoint was at epoch 27, while training continued to epoch 29.
record.problems: Only one training run with random seed 42 is reported; results are point estimates. Training stopped at 30 epochs maximum with early stopping, and the study did not compare training error across sizes or initialization choices. Image-level rather than patient-level partitioning may place images from one patient in multiple partitions.
record.rows_left_out: none; the selected training-accuracy values in Table V are recorded separately by epoch.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100, corrupted or random labels, sufficiently large model comparisons, and effects of model size, stopping time or regularization. Final fixed-checkpoint training-set accuracy with augmentation and dropout disabled is not reported.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths and shortcut configurations; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Comparative initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery and divergence.
Matched training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with and without batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: All ten rows describe one training trajectory, not independent replications. Training metrics are reported during a recipe with stochastic augmentation and dropout; they do not establish the final model's error on unaugmented training images in inference mode. The results do not challenge the sufficiently-large-network CIFAR claim.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
